query: Why have I become so cynical?

per_question.q: Which page leaves the reader more in charge of changing this?
per_question.why: In Page A, the seminar link sits tucked inside the callout box as an optional exploration, leaving the transition directly into the reader's self-reflection rather than creating a speedbump.

per_question.q: Which page asks less of the reader before it has earned it?
per_question.why: Page B places an external seminar pitch link directly in the body text before the opening story has even begun, asking for commercial trust prematurely.

per_question.q: Which page treats the reader as the person who does the work, rather than as someone who has to be sent somewhere?
per_question.why: Page B pulls the reader out of the narrative right into an external seminar link before they have read a single full section.

per_question.q: Which page gives the reader more room to decide for themselves what to do next?
per_question.why: In Page A, confining the seminar link to the bottom of the callout card preserves the open space of the prose narrative immediately following.

per_question.q: Which page puts the author's own history to better use for the reader?
per_question.why: Both versions share identical author history paragraphs, but Page A frames the narrative without an awkward standalone promo link preceding the introduction.

per_question.q: Which page makes the first screen feel more like the reader's own words?
per_question.why: Page A keeps the introductory dialogue flow intact; in Page B, the standalone link between the callout box and 'A friend tells you...' creates an intrusive commercial voice.

per_question.q: Which page's opening is easier to read straight through without being interrupted?
per_question.why: Page A flows cleanly from the identify-box directly into the opening narrative scenario, whereas Page B is jarringly interrupted by a freestanding link paragraph.

per_question.q: Which page makes a reader likelier to think "that is me" in the first thirty seconds?
per_question.why: The transition from the four internal sentences directly into the vignette about a friend getting back together with an ex is unbroken by promotional link text in Page A.

per_question.q: Which page keeps its argument moving without a detour that breaks the thread?
per_question.why: Page B inserts a standalone paragraph containing an external seminar link immediately before the opening illustration, stalling momentum.

per_question.q: Which page makes it easier to follow the line from the question at the top to the answer?
per_question.why: In Page B, keeping the identify-box strictly to the four self-talk lines without an embedded link keeps the box itself purely focused on definitions.

A: The callout box mixes diagnostic self-talk quotes with an external promotional link at the bottom.
B: Dangling a standalone seminar link between the identify-box and the opening story creates an abrupt interruption to the narrative flow.

first_screen: Page A leaves the reader more in charge because the link to the external seminar is neatly contained within the identify box rather than sitting as a prominent, disruptive speedbump in the main reading column right above the opening narrative.
provenance: Both pages have identical text and structure, but Page A maintains superior document cohesion by keeping promotional material scoped inside UI containers.
